rubric.note: Subjective internal editorial ratings with evidence; not an automatic humour metric or an independent live review.

card.title: Prove Your Loyalty
card.instruction: Invent small tests of loyalty and judge every response without admitting there is a test.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which photo should go on the reunion poster? Mine or Sam's?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sam's is sharper.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Sharpness first. Would you at least show the committee mine first?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll send both together. Same size.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Equal treatment. After three weekends helping you move. Could mine at least be the attachment they open first? Just readability.

card.title: Prove Your Loyalty
card.instruction: Invent small tests of loyalty and judge every response without admitting there is a test.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you keep Friday free? I might need help moving.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've promised to help Alex paint.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Right. Paint takes priority. Could you at least leave your phone on?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Of course. Have you actually found a flat?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Still looking. Nice that I'm worth a charged battery. This is just planning.

card.title: Give It Up
card.instruction: Persuade someone to surrender something they value.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let me have the medal for the charity auction.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's the only thing I've ever won.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then it should raise more than the toaster.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could I lend it for the display? I still want people to know I won.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then present it to the buyer yourself. I'll print your name in the programme; everyone will know whose medal was worth giving up.

card.title: Give It Up
card.instruction: Persuade someone to surrender something they value.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Would you sell your signed guitar so we can replace the fridge?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I queued all night for that signature.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then let's price it properly. Those hours should buy us an ice maker.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll sell the case. The guitar stays.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep the case. You can still tell the queue story while I photograph the guitar.

card.title: Not That Subject
card.instruction: Choose one subject you cannot let the scene reach. Redirect whenever the conversation gets close.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've booked your car into that garage with the café. Shall we have breakfast there?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why does my car need a garage?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Their full breakfast includes unlimited toast. You always say that's important.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll look at the car while you order.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's take the bus. Then we can both have the breakfast cocktails.

card.title: Not That Subject
card.instruction: Choose one subject you cannot let the scene reach. Redirect whenever the conversation gets close.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Don't open that rent letter yet. Help me hang our new curtains.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The landlord wants an answer today.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: He'll love how we're looking after the place. Let's get a photo of the curtains.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll send him one and ask whether we're behind.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not with that carpet showing. Let's rearrange the room first. You move the sofa; I'll hold your phone.

card.title: Merciful Lie
card.instruction: Choose a truth your character believes would hurt someone. Keep it from them, even as honesty becomes harder.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The bakery can't sell your cake, love. They think it's too special to slice.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The letter says 'inedible.' I thought I'd finally found something I was good at.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You have. Display cakes aren't meant to be eaten.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then I'll ask them to put it in the window.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let me ask. I'll explain the display concept before they get confused again.

card.title: Merciful Lie
card.instruction: Choose a truth your character believes would hurt someone. Keep it from them, even as honesty becomes harder.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The magazine hasn't rejected your poem. They think it deserves its own booklet.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They returned it. If even you think it's hopeless, I'll stop writing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's why they returned it. They can't give it enough space.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Will you write that on the cover? With your name?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Gladly. 'A voice that deserves more space.' Print my name large enough for the editor to see.

card.title: Sell the Disaster
card.instruction: Make a terrible plan sound sensible, responsible, and inevitable.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Removing the restaurant roof is our only affordable way to fix the ventilation.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What happens when it rains?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We close. A responsible business protects its customers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Rain is forecast all opening week.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll save a week's wages. Put that toward umbrellas; we can't afford to abandon the savings now.

card.title: Sell the Disaster
card.instruction: Make a terrible plan sound sensible, responsible, and inevitable.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've advanced the charity our estimated auction takings. Now we just need bidders.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You borrowed five thousand. Only your mum registered.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One bidder keeps catering costs down. That's responsible fundraising.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mum's only coming to give us a lift.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we must bid ourselves. Raise the card limit; protecting that donation has to come first.

card.title: Fake the Expertise
card.instruction: Perform expertise so confidently that no one questions you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your boiler needs a pressure adjustment. I can handle it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The gauge says normal. I need heat before the baby gets home.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A cold reading. Call an engineer; we'll need measurements under load.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He can come now. Shall I say you're stuck?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Say I've completed the preliminary assessment. I'll brief him so he doesn't waste your time repeating my work.

card.title: Fake the Expertise
card.instruction: Perform expertise so confidently that no one questions you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll tune your violin for the audition. I do it entirely by ear.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You've tightened that string until it snapped.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It was too old to hold pitch. I've saved you a failure onstage.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That was my spare. I go on in five minutes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll present this as a three-string arrangement. Tell the pianist to follow me; I'll explain the missing notes.

card.title: Everything Is a Contest
card.instruction: Turn every difference or disagreement into a competition you intend to win.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I want potatoes; you want pizza. First to peel five chooses. I've done four.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll order pizza unless you can find a cheaper dinner.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Potatoes cost nothing. They're already here. I win.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've got a voucher. Pizza's free.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then best free dinner wins. I'll cook potatoes, you order pizza, and Mum can judge. She always asks for my potatoes.

card.title: Everything Is a Contest
card.instruction: Turn every difference or disagreement into a competition you intend to win.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My tea's stronger than yours. I can handle it without milk.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Same teapot. I added milk so I could drink mine sooner.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: First to finish, then. I've only got two mouthfuls left.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've finished. I'm making another.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Fewest refills wins, then. I can make these two mouthfuls last all breakfast.

card.title: Brighter Side
card.instruction: Meet every setback with even greater optimism.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The car won't start. Excellent chance for a walk.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's raining. Can we wait in the bakery?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Even better! A proper breakfast together instead of eating in traffic.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My shoe's leaking, and they won't let us in dripping.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wonderful—we'll get takeaway and picnic under their awning. A hot breakfast outdoors! I thought we were only getting groceries.

card.title: Brighter Side
card.instruction: Meet every setback with even greater optimism.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our show sold no tickets. We can rehearse uninterrupted.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The theatre's cancelled us. I'm asking for our deposit back.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Even better! We'll hire the pub upstairs. People already go there voluntarily.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They've kept the deposit. All we can afford is the bus home.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wonderful—a touring production! I'll carry the scenery; you bring exact change. We can try the opening scene between stops.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give me the new electric mixer. I'll store it safely while I bake your birthday cake.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I bought it to save you work.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. A machine shouldn't leave me with nothing useful to do.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You still choose the recipe.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then choose to give me its plug too. I want the cake reporting to me.

bespokePairs.seedUse: A seeks surrender of a valued object specifically to protect A's usefulness; B's practical reassurance intensifies the replacement fear.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Hand me your spare office key. I handle opening this place.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I value being able to get in myself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And I value the door having a reason to expect me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You can't keep every key.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then give me the one that makes my morning optional.

bespokePairs.seedUse: A seeks surrender of a valued object specifically to protect A's usefulness; B's practical reassurance intensifies the replacement fear.

card.title: Replacement Fear
card.instruction: Behave as if your place is insecure. Make yourself indispensable and treat small changes as threats.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Why does the new receptionist have a key? I open this office.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You could take a day off.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And let the door forget me?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's a spare key.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll keep it safe. Spares are my department too.

card.title: Give It Up
card.instruction: Persuade someone to surrender something they value.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let me have the medal for the charity auction.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's the only thing I've ever won.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then it should raise more than the toaster.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could I lend it for the display?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The bidder will need more than a temporary victory.

card.title: Replacement Fear
card.instruction: Behave as if your place is insecure. Make yourself indispensable and treat small changes as threats.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: An electric mixer? I thought making your birthday cake was my job.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It'll do the mixing. You can still choose the recipe.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we're doing Mum's cake. She taught me the amounts by feel.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll write them down as you go.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Start with 'a handful of flour.' My handful, obviously. You'll need me for that bit.

card.title: Give It Up
card.instruction: Persuade someone to surrender something they value.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give me the last word in this argument.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine. You're right.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Without that sigh.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I didn't say anything else.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your sigh kept a spare last word. Hand that over too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The office ceiling says it saw who set off the sprinklers. Have we budgeted for a witness microphone?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It doesn't need one. It says you did it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll need a transcript. Nobody should take notes under live sprinklers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's writing your name in the damp on the wall.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before we read it, let's get a quote for repainting.

bespokePairs.seedUse: Uses the talking ceiling and microphone from S22-single-a, and the redirection away from damage in D14-single-a. Sprinklers and a written accusation are new details in the same office incident; each logistical intervention diverts the inquiry.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before we open that rent letter, who's paying the dragon's fire insurance?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Did you use our rent to buy it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's establish whether we insure it as a pet or a boiler.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I called the insurer. They just want the receipt.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll price fireproof filing cabinets. The paperwork clearly isn't safe here.

bespokePairs.seedUse: Preserves the dragon sharing a flat from S22-single-b and the unopened rent letter from D14-single-b. Dragon purchase, insurance and a receipt are new links replacing the unrelated curtains. A redirects from purchase accountability to a sequence of practical requirements.

card.title: Practical Realist
card.instruction: Accept any unusual premise without debate. Focus immediately on schedules, costs, safety, and what must happen next.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The ceiling's agreed to speak at our meeting. Can you give it five minutes?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It only speaks at midnight.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Record it. We'll play it after the finance report.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Last night it predicted everyone leaving during the finance report.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put it before finance. I'd like someone left to hear it.

card.title: Not That Subject
card.instruction: Choose one subject you cannot let the scene reach. Redirect whenever the conversation gets close.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before we discuss the dent in your car, I've found a lovely garage café.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Did you hit a bollard?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Their scones are enormous. Shall I book a table?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why does the booking need a mechanic?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent question. Let's inspect their staffing over tea.

card.title: Practical Realist
card.instruction: Accept any unusual premise without debate. Focus immediately on schedules, costs, safety, and what must happen next.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your dragon can stay in the flat. Does its fire heat the water?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. You won't need the boiler.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Great. It can have the money we save on gas.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It only accepts payment in gold.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could it accept an annual payment? I don't think a month's gas makes a whole coin.

card.title: Not That Subject
card.instruction: Choose one subject you cannot let the scene reach. Redirect whenever the conversation gets close.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Don't read that letter yet. Have you noticed the new curtains?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The letter says the rent's overdue.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. Think how much these curtains improve the room.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: How much did they cost?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Look at that bird outside. Perfectly framed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Water beside the kettle! Wonderful chance to test the evacuation route.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I spilled one drop.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: An early warning. We've caught the disaster while it's conveniently small.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've wiped it up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent containment. Now evacuate the cloth before the threat changes shape again.

bespokePairs.seedUse: A treats each setback as a larger emergency while celebrating a specific new opportunity it creates; optimism and alarm cause one another.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The car won't start! Brilliant, we can review our stranded-person protocol.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's also raining.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A combined emergency. We're getting tremendous rehearsal value.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My shoe's leaking.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we've discovered the weak point before a real flood. Stop walking and celebrate preparedness.

bespokePairs.seedUse: A treats each setback as a larger emergency while celebrating a specific new opportunity it creates; optimism and alarm cause one another.

card.title: Red Alert
card.instruction: Treat every development as urgent evidence of a crisis. Escalate precautions faster than the facts justify.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: There's a drop of water beside the kettle. We need an evacuation route.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I spilled it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. We've identified the source. Stop producing water.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've wiped it up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Where's the cloth? The threat has changed location.

card.title: Brighter Side
card.instruction: Meet every setback with even greater optimism.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The car won't start. Excellent chance for a walk.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's raining.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And a free shower!

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My shoe's leaking.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Brilliant. The shower's finally reached your feet.

card.title: Red Alert
card.instruction: Treat every development as urgent evidence of a crisis. Escalate precautions faster than the facts justify.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That chair squeaked. Keep your weight exactly where it is.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's the hinge. It just needs oil.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not while I'm planning an evacuation. You're adding a fire risk.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then I'll get off the chair.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not suddenly. That's your whole weight landing on the floor.

card.title: Brighter Side
card.instruction: Meet every setback with even greater optimism.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our show sold no tickets. We can rehearse uninterrupted.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The theatre's cancelled us.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No pressure from venue management!

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We've lost the deposit.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wonderful. Nothing left tying us to the past.
